topic_ko: 사람들은 기본 설정을 그대로 따르는 경향이 있으므로, 더 친환경적인 선택지를 디폴트로 바꾸면 자연스럽게 더 바람직한 행동으로 유도할 수 있다

passage: A default is the choice that takes effect when a person simply does nothing at all.
Anyone may step away from it, yet very few people ever bother to do so.
Changing a preset demands a conscious effort, and we prefer to keep whatever we already hold.
A preset also feels like advice, so refusing it can make us look like poor citizens.
That is why turning the greener option into the preset quietly moves people toward better habits.
One American university made double-sided printing standard and saved roughly 62 million sheets in three years.
A delivery app made plastic cutlery something users must request, after learning over 90% of customers did not want it.
Since each of us designs choices for others now and then, learning this skill is worth the trouble.
choices: the environmental damage caused by careless university printing
how presetting the better option quietly guides people's behavior
why consumers should demand more options from delivery services
the legal limits placed on companies that change their settings

theme.explanation_ko: 디폴트의 정의와 관성 심리, 러트거스와 배달 앱 사례, 마지막 선택 설계자 당부까지 모두 '기본 설정을 더 나은 쪽으로 바꾸어 행동을 이끈다'로 모인다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 인쇄로 인한 환경 피해가 아니라 절약 사례이다. ③ 소비자가 선택지를 요구하라는 주장은 없다. ④ 법적 규제는 언급되지 않는다. ⑤ 새로운 인쇄 기술이 아니라 설정 변경이 핵심이다.

passage: An option that applies all by itself, unless the chooser acts, is called a default.
Nobody is forced to accept it, but almost everyone does.
We cling to what we already have because switching costs us mental effort.
On top of that, a preset quietly signals that someone recommends this very choice.
So when the eco-friendly option becomes the preset, sustainable behavior follows automatically.
Rutgers University proved it in 2008 by making double-sided printing the standard for every printer.
A food delivery company proved it again by asking users to request forks and spoons instead of receiving them by default.
Small changes in the starting point can reshape what millions of people end up doing.

gist.distractor_ko: ① 교육이 아니라 설정 변경이 방법이다. ② 선택지 수를 줄이자는 말은 없다. ④ 자유는 이미 보장되어 있다는 전제일 뿐 주장이 아니다. ⑤ 규정으로 통제한 것이 아니라 기본값만 바꾸었다.

passage: When a chooser does nothing, one option still takes effect, and that option is the default.
Opting out is always allowed, yet the pull of the preset is remarkably strong.
People are ruled by a desire to keep what they hold, since any change costs deliberate effort.
A default also carries a hint of endorsement, so leaving it can feel slightly irresponsible.
Make the greener path the preset, then, and sustainable behavior arrives without persuasion.
In 2008 Rutgers University set double-sided printing as standard and saved about 62 million sheets within three years.
A delivery app flipped cutlery to opt-in after a survey showed more than 90% of its customers never needed it.
All of us design choices for someone at some point, so this quiet tool is worth learning.
